title: Turn AI ambition into real business value with Power Platform
summary: Learn how Microsoft Power Platform helps businesses innovate with AI agents, low-code apps, intelligent automation, and enhanced governance.
body_markdown:
Last month at the[Power Platform Community Conference](https://www.microsoft.com/power-platform/blog/2026/10/29/built-by-makers-five-years-of-power-platform-community-conference/) , 9,000 makers joined us not just to learn what’s next, but to help shape it. That spirit of co-creation reflects something bigger about Microsoft Power Platform: the people building the future of business applications are already helping define what comes next.


At[Microsoft Ignite 2026](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/home) , we’re building on that momentum and showing why organizations running on[Power Platform](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform) are entering the agentic era from a position of strength.


I want to start this Ignite with a bold claim, one that I deeply believe in and hold with strong conviction: **there has never been a better time to be a Power Platform customer than right now.**


We continue to strengthen the tools customers rely on today while creating new ways to build for what comes next. Our focus extends across the solution lifecycle, from building and evolving applications to maintaining and supporting them over time. In this post, I want to share where the platform is today, the principles guiding our decisions, and what we’re building for the future.


[Explore Microsoft Power Platform](https://www.microsoft.com/power-platform)


## Building a stronger, growing platform


Today, 80 million people use Power Platform every month and the intensity of the use is growing: over the last year, daily active users of[Power Apps](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-apps) grew 20%,[Power Automate](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-automate) flow runs grew 20%, and AI usage in Power Apps doubled. This momentum gives us a strong foundation to keep improving the platform and help you unlock new value from the solutions you’ve already built.


The analysts recognize Microsoft as a leader in next-generation application development platforms as well:[Microsoft named a Leader in two evaluations of next-generation app development platforms](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/blog/2026/10/22/microsoft-named-a-leader-in-two-evaluations-of-next-generation-app-development-platforms/) .


In the spirit of co-creation, here are the four operating principles that guide our product and engineering decisions:


1. **Lead with the power of the platform** . Apps, flows, portals, data, and agents are stronger together on one secure, governed platform.
2. **Deliver high-quality products** . Performance and reliability matter, and so does the quality of every experience and every customer journey.
3. **Bring AI to you, on your terms** . You decide where, when and how to use AI, and when to pay for it.
4. **Protect the investments you’ve already made** . Innovation should make the platform better, not force you to start over.


These principles shape our strategy and how we execute it, organized around four pillars. In the rest of this post, I’ll share what we’ve delivered in each one:


1. Improve the quality of the platform
2. Build with hybrid teams of humans and agents
3. Bring agents into the flow of work
4. Unlock the value of what you’ve built


## Pillar 1: Improving the quality of the platform


Everything we build starts with you. Power Platform is shaped by our customers and community, and you’ve told us clearly what matters most: production-ready solutions that are fast, reliable, deliver rich experiences, and are simple to build. You’ve invested years in the apps, flows and sites that run your business. Our job is to help **protect those investments** and **move them forward** by giving you the best platform we can.


A strong platform matters even more in the age of AI! First, it gives AI solid building blocks: when the controls, views, data, and building tools are strong, AI has a better foundation to build on. Second, once that platform is in place, AI can help take it even further.


You can see this commitment in what we’ve delivered. This year we shipped more than 130 new capabilities, and 65% of them focused on improving quality and experience. We also retired 24 features to focus on what matters most to you, helping create a cleaner, more streamlined platform. A few highlights:


- **Faster performance** . Compared to previous versions the new canvas controls are designed for better performance, model-driven apps load faster, and mobile apps start up faster.
- **Improved experiences for the people using your solutions** . New modern controls expand what’s possible in canvas apps. Model-driven apps gain new views such as calendar, cards, and timeline views.[Mobile apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/mobile/run-powerapps-on-mobile) get native experiences, and cloud flows can connect to on-premises systems with fewer steps.
- **More reliable** . We’ve reduced customer incidents in canvas apps, and offline sync is more dependable, with sync that now keeps working when the app is in the background.
- **Simpler for makers** . Canvas apps gain a detachable formula bar, a delegation limit extended to 10,000 items, and a grid container that simplifies responsive layouts. Inline views in Power Automate cloud flows, along with new[Flowchart](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/desktop-flows/flowchart-flow-designer) and Flow Map views in[Power Automate desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/desktop-flows/install) , make it easier understand and evolve your flows.


That’s a lot, and it’s still only a fraction of the improvements we’re bringing to the solutions you already have and the new ones you’ll build. Quality is never done. Your expectations keep rising, and so will our bar. Thank you for building this platform with us.


## Pillar 2: Build with hybrid teams of humans and agents


With Power Platform, makers can build with hybrid teams of humans and agents that work together. Makers bring in agents where and when they need them, deciding what to use AI for and when to pay for it. Here’s what makes it different:


- **Agents when you want them, and only then** . Agents can be helpful collaborators that go beyond building, analyzing a solution, refactoring it, and more. Bring in agents when they help and remove them when you no longer need them. You decide where your tokens go.
- **For new solutions and the ones you already have** . Agents can work on the apps and flows you’ve built over the years, not just new ones, so your existing investments keep moving forward.
- **Your work keeps going** . If you run out of tokens, your team can keep building with the improved tools described above. AI can speed up the work, but you don’t have to depend on it.


On top of that, makers get the best of both worlds: the power of a coding agent, and a low-code solution as the result. Through our model context protocol (MCP) servers, agents build with Power Platform controls and components, so you know what you’re getting. What they create can be opened, edited, and evolved by others on your team, and it can be managed, governed, and secured just like the rest of your Power Platform solutions.


Professional developers can start in[GitHub Copilot](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/github/copilot) or other supported coding agents. Makers can work in dedicated studios within Power Platform products, and business users can build from[Microsoft Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot) and[Cowork](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/features/cowork) .


**G&J Pepsi,** the largest independent Pepsi bottler in the United States, shows what this looks like in practice. Over the past decade, the company has used Power Platform to bring application experiences, data and business rules together for teams across the organization. With hybrid authoring, its makers can bring agents into those same solutions and keep evolving them, without rebuilding from the ground up.


## Pillar 3: Bring agents into the flow of work


Every solution you’ve built holds what makes your business run: your data, processes, and rules. Now we’re bringing more value to the people who use those solutions every day, without rebuilding your apps.


For example, Copilot in model-driven or canvas apps brings the full power of Copilot, including your previous conversations and agents, right into your apps. It’s grounded in your app, using the data, context, and business processes behind it. Here’s what that means for you:


- **More value from the apps you already have** .[Copilot in model-driven apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/user/use-microsoft-365-copilot-model-driven-apps) became generally available in April, and[Copilot in canvas apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/add-ai-copilot) reaches general availability this November. Your existing apps can do more without being rebuilt.
- **Tailored to your business** . Makers can shape the experience with suggested prompts, app-specific context and actions, so users go from insight to action in one place.
- **Your rules stay in place** . Copilot works within the app’s existing data access and permissions, helping IT keep the security and governance it needs to scale.
- **Connected to Microsoft 365** . The business context in your apps connects with the productivity tools people use every day, and we’re working to make it easier to bring Copilot into more of the apps and sites you build.


## Pillar 4: Unlock value of everything you’ve built


Agents are only as good as the business context they have. Over the years, your apps, flows, and sites have captured the context of how your business runs: the processes, business rules, approvals, and institutional knowledge that agents need to do meaningful work.


With[Business Applications in Work IQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/business-applications-work-iq) , we’re helping you unlock that value. Your apps, flows, and sites can become a tool for agents across Microsoft Copilot, Cowork,[Copilot Studio](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/products/copilot-studio) , GitHub Copilot, and the custom agents you build. Here’s why it matters:


- **No need to open the app.** Agents use the context and capabilities of your solutions directly, in the places people already work.
- **No rebuilding.** The solutions you already have can be made available to agents as they are.
- **Governed like the rest of your solutions.** Agents you authorize work within your existing permissions and governance controls.


Consider G&J Pepsi again. The same app that unified its frontline sales operations can now give Microsoft Copilot business context and capabilities directly. An investment made a decade ago becomes an advantage in the agentic era.


## A platform built for today and what comes next


If there’s one thing I want you to take away, it’s this: **you don’t have to start over to move forward.**


The apps, flows, and sites you’ve built aren’t just investments we’re committed to preserving. They’re the foundation we’re building on. What changes is what those investments can do: they can become faster and more reliable. Agents help you analyze, fix, and evolve them. They can bring new value to the people who use them and give agents the context to do meaningful work. When you’re ready to build something new, the same hybrid teams of humans and agents are there too, in the tools you already use.


All of this runs on a platform used by more than 80 million people every month. It’s designed to bring together the security, governance, operational management, and availability enterprises need across the full solution lifecycle, from building to running and evolving.


The opportunity ahead isn’t simply to adopt more AI. It’s to put AI to work with the context of your business, build on the solutions you’ve already invested in, and help people move from insight to action.


That’s what we’re building with Power Platform, and we’re just getting started.


## Accelerate your innovation


Build intelligent apps and automate workflows with AI-powered, low-code tools from Power Platform.


[Get started](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform)
